experiment.name: phase9_procedural_transfer_recovery_v2_1
experiment.primary_failure: Oracle-RAG capable student fails answerable Real-RAG procedures
experiment.research_question: How much of the Oracle-to-Real procedural gap is retrieval collision versus learned evidence-binding weakness?

retrieval.policy: When an explicit locator appears in the query, suppress passages with conflicting explicit locators when an exact match exists. Deduplicate identical procedure rules. Recalibrate answerability after changing selection.

data.primary_pattern: target record + shuffled near-identical sibling records
data.gold_policy: deterministic computed labels; implicit ties forbidden; explicit tie-break procedures tested separately
data.preservation_policy: mix a deterministic train-only slice of the previous broad Phase 9 curriculum; never draw preservation examples from dev/test

training.strategy: two-stage focused recovery; no broad hyperparameter sweep

stage_a.name: collision_binding
stage_a.purpose: teach exact record binding under sibling collisions

stage_b.name: consolidation
stage_b.purpose: retain procedural recovery while preserving supported/unsupported/conflict/social behavior

training.rank32_policy: Do not run by default. Consider only after the focused rank-16 path shows genuine training underfit rather than a retrieval/prompt failure.

selection.release_policy: Separate retrieval-policy gain from training-only gain. Prefer positive procedural gain with lower preservation loss. Human approval remains required.
selection.blocker: A student that remains at zero correct answerable procedures after query-aware retrieval and recovery training is not eligible for downstream structural optimization.

other_students.policy: Do not retrain all students immediately. First establish the mechanism on the current high-value student. Afterward run one or two controlled replication students with the same fixed v2.1 recipe to test generality.
